newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Barito to venture into coal, agribusiness.
newsitem.headline: Barito to venture into coal, agribusiness.

text.p: Indonesian timber giant PT Barito Pacific Timber plans to mine coal and to plant oil palms as part of the company's long-term diversification plans, a Barito official said on Thursday.

"For the long term we have decided to broaden our revenue base by moving into coal mining and agribusiness. We have established three subsidiaries for coal mining," Barito director Susana Susanto told a brefing.
"We have applied for licences for coal mining, covering 97,000 hectares in Sumatra," she said.
"For agribusiness, two subsidiaries have been established for the production of palm oil. Applications have been submitted for licences for 48,000 hectares in Kalimantan," she said.
She said Barito saw coal as being an important energy source in the future, adding that demand for crude palm oil, which is used to produce cooking oil and cosmestics, was rising.
"We envisage that diversification into agribusiness, mainly palm oil, will further add value to the company," she said.
Barito is one of the biggest wood producers in Indonesia.
